source_snapshot.title: Dubai sets new speed limits on five roads under traffic safety drive
source_snapshot.text: Dubai's traffic authorities are reducing the speed limits on three roads and increasing them on two others, as part of the Dubai Traffic Safety Strategy. The changes have been authorised by the emirate's Roads and Transport Authority and Dubai Police. The speed limit has been raised from 60kph to 70kph on Al Mustaqbal Street, between Sheikh Rashid Street and Al Meydan Street, and on Latifa bint Hamdan Street, between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road. On Al Asayel Street, between Oud Metha Street and Al Meydan Street, the limit will be increased from 60kph to 80kph. The limit on Al Rebat Street, between Marrakech Street and Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Road, will be reduced from 100kph to 90kph, and from 80kph to 70kph on Sheikh Sabah Al Ahmad Al Jaber Al Sabah Street, between 2nd December Street and Khalid bin Al Waleed Street. The changes will come into effect from November 1 and are in line with a major drive by Dubai transport authorities to boost road safety and improve traffic flow to keep pace with the needs of a growing population.

claims.claim: From November 1, speed limits will change on five roads in Dubai.
On Al Mustaqbal Street and Latifa bint Hamdan Street, speed limits will increase from 60 to 70 km/h.
On Al Asayel Street, speed limit will increase to 80 km/h.
On Al Rebat Street, speed limit will decrease from 100 to 90 km/h.
On Sheikh Sabah Al Ahmad Al Jaber Al Sabah Street, speed limit will decrease from 80 to 70 km/h.
The changes were approved by the Roads and Transport Authority and Dubai Police as part of the traffic safety strategy.
